title: Positional and incremental PID
equipment: Industrial positioning table and recirculating water heater
physicalPurpose: Use one production controller for P, PI, PD, and PID without allowing an invalid state-update realization to be selected.
principalTechnique: Positional, incremental, and combined PID realization
objective: Explain and verify why Control.PID uses positional realization without integral action and incremental realization with integral action.

simplifications: The two deterministic simulator plants isolate controller realization; they are not physical-plant evidence.
The rejected incremental-P recurrence is a calculation-only diagnostic and is never connected to either plant.
The lesson holds process inputs unchanged for the exact two-update gain-change comparison before allowing either plant to advance.

baseline.limitation: At unchanged nonzero error, the rejected incremental-P recurrence calculates zero output increment and remains at its arbitrary retained output after a proportional-gain change.

change.decision: Let the shipped controller select positional P when integral gain is zero and incremental PI when integral gain is nonzero; do not expose a user form switch.

disturbances: Proportional gain changes from 4 to 8 while error and plant feedback are held unchanged for one update

acceptance.window: one 20 ms update at unchanged 0.5 rad error
first update after gain changes from 4 to 8
one 20 ms update at unchanged 15 degC error

abortPredicates: Any plant or controller value is nonfinite
Table position, torque, water temperature, or heater power leaves its declared hard limit
The rejected diagnostic is connected to a plant command
safety.restorationMode: Manual mode with zero motor torque and zero heater power
simulationOnlyRestrictions: These results do not qualify physical drive startup, heater protection, mode transfer, or gain changes.

video.viewerOutcome: Predict and verify why one production PID selects positional realization for P or PD and incremental realization for PI or PID.

learning.context: The positioning table needs P action while the water heater needs PI action, but operators should use the same production Control.PID block for both.
learning.reason: Lesson 25 showed that a digital controller is a recurrence with retained state. A single recurrence is not valid for every P, PI, PD, and PID combination.
theory: Positional realization calculates the complete output from present terms. Incremental or velocity realization adds term increments to the retained previous output.

At unchanged error the proportional increment is zero. Pure incremental P can therefore retain an arbitrary output and ignore a proportional-gain change, while positional P immediately recalculates the physically required output.

With nonzero integral action, the integral increment continually changes output in response to persistent error. Retaining output also supports practical tracking, clamping anti-windup, and bumpless parameter changes.

Control.PID selects positional realization when integral gain is zero and incremental realization when integral gain is nonzero. This realization choice is different from parallel, ideal, or series parameter forms.
learning.workedPrediction: At constant error 0.5 rad, positional P torque changes from 2 to 4 N m when gain changes from 4 to 8 N m/rad. The rejected incremental-P error change is zero, so its arbitrary 1 N m retained output does not change. At 15 degC heater error, integral gain 0.8 %/(degC*s), and 0.02 s sample interval, the expected PI output increment is 0.24%.
practicalPreparation: Bind both plant SP, PV, and MV signals; both gains; the rejected diagnostic; positional prediction; selected-form indicators; limits; update time; and simulation evidence label.
Restore both plants to the declared initial state and freeze error, previous error, sample interval, bias, limits, and retained output for the exact gain-change comparison.
learning.baseline: Run the rejected incremental-P diagnostic at constant error and prove that changing gain from 4 to 8 leaves its arbitrary 1 N m retained output unchanged.
learning.change: Run the same gain change through Control.PID with zero integral gain on the positioning table, then repeat the unchanged-signal gain change with nonzero integral gain on the heater.
learning.comparison: Compare the immediate positional-P output change, rejected incremental-P state, and PI output change after subtracting the predicted integral increment over the same one-update window.
learning.validation: Require positional P to change from 2 to 4 N m, rejected incremental P to remain at 1 N m, PI discontinuity after the expected 0.24% integral increment to be zero within tolerance, and all applied outputs to remain finite and inside limits.
learning.explanation: A state-update formula is part of controller behavior, not an interchangeable coding style. The presence of integral action determines which recurrence preserves the required control meaning and practical transitions.
learning.transfer: Use one Control.PID instance for P, PI, PD, or PID and let its integral gain select the valid internal realization. Lesson 27 introduces initialization, manual, tracking, disabled, and transition behavior.
